name: Scopa Corse
description: Scopa Corse is the Corsican variant of Scopa, played with a 36-card Italian deck (no 2s). Players capture table cards by matching rank or by sum; unlike basic Scopa, capturing is optional. First to 21 points wins.

content.text: Scopa Corse is the Corsican variant of Scopa, played with a 36-card Italian deck (no 2s). Players capture table cards by matching rank or by sum; unlike basic Scopa, capturing is optional. First to 21 points wins.

Scopa originated in Italy and was especially popular in Naples by the 18th century; it spread to Corsica where it is played as Scopa Corse with a 36-card deck (twos removed) and optional capture. The Corsican form is played alongside related games in Spain and North Africa and is documented with EREDI-brand rules; the stripped deck adds tactical depth by making sums of 7 harder to form.
36-card Italian deck: each suit has Ace, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, Jack, Queen, King (no 2s).
3 cards to each player, 4 face-up on the table. Two players: next three deals 3 cards each, last two deals 4 cards each. Four players: second deal 3 each, third deal 2 each.
